sources.note: Nothing. Lists Pu Ko as Southwestern Tai, ISO [puk] retired 2017, 'no substantive evidence that the language ever existed'.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2016. Change Request Number 2016-011: Retire [puk] Pu Ko (submitted by Nate Cheeseman, Payap University, 2016-05-16; adopted 2017-01-31). Dallas: SIL International. 5 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. It is a code-retirement form: reason 'There is no evidence that the language exists' (p. 2, sec. 3a); rationale (p. 2, sec. 3c) quotes Fennig ('for over 60 years, we have gained virtually no knowledge about this language') and Hammarström 2015 Appendix B: 'Pu Ko [puk] is listed as a SW Tai language in Laos without a speaker estimate or a location. No such language or ethnicity could be found in the comprehensive ethnic survey of Laos (Schliesinger 2003c:287)'; adds that the name resembles Thai พวกเขา 'they'.

sources.citation: Hammarström, Harald. 2015. Ethnologue 16/17/18th editions: A comprehensive review. Language 91(3): 723-737. DOI 10.1353/lan.2015.0038.
sources.note: Nothing; main article (green-OA copy from MPG PuRe) does not name Pu Ko.
